claims.text: Simultaneous mechanical wear and corrosive attack induces an ultra-nanostructured surface layer in high-entropy alloys through dynamic grain refinement.
Wear-induced deformation causes local or partial amorphization of the surface.
The wear-generated surface layer is chemically homogenized.
The ultra-nanostructured surface layer functions as a dense passive barrier.
The surface barrier is self-healing or self-renewing during wear.
The ultra-nanostructured layer accommodates mechanical deformation and reduces mechanical material removal.
The dense surface layer impedes penetration of the corrosive electrolyte or aggressive ions.
The wear-generated layer stabilizes passivity and reduces localized corrosion, including pitting.
CoCrFeMnNi can have an initially coarse-grained, single-phase state before deformation.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion produces a finer and more continuous passive layer than pure wear in an inert environment or static corrosion.
Formation of the refined surface layer leads to a lower wear rate.
Formation of the refined surface layer leads to a lower friction coefficient.
The dynamically formed surface layer improves corrosion resistance under simultaneous wear-corrosion, as indicated by lower corrosion-current density and higher impedance.
The beneficial dynamically formed nanostructured layer is absent or less pronounced during pure wear in an inert environment or static immersion.
The proposed mechanism operates under moderate mechanical stress and corrosiveness when the dynamic layer can form and persist.
Excessive load or corrosive aggressiveness causes the mechanism to fail by exceeding the capacity for passive-film regeneration.
The mechanism may fail in alloy compositions that do not favor rapid grain refinement.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator identifies the ultra-nanocrystalline/amorphous top layer itself as the passive film, whereas the mechanism treats that layer as something that stabilizes a separate passive film.

The mechanism attributes formation of the refined layer to wear-induced deformation, but the baseline states that the beneficial layer is absent or less pronounced under pure wear; the cited CoCrFeMnNi evidence specifically reports formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer during wear in an inert environment.
